matches.rationale: Ground truth concerns overstatement of 94% compression with adversarial accuracy improvements in the Abstract conflicting with detailed results. No finding identifies this specific cross-section inconsistency between Abstract claims and empirical tables regarding compression-robustness trade-offs.

pred_id 2 identifies the exact discrepancy in Proposition 2's condition number bound: the statement claims κ(S) ≤ exp(R(S)/(2σ_r(S))) but the proof derives exp(R(S)/(√2 σ_r(S)²)), matching the ground truth's claim of weakened/erroneous relationship. pred_id 4 confirms equation (4) is missing, supporting the inconsistency.

Ground truth concerns omission of hyperparameter tuning details (β, learning rate schedules, augmentation) preventing reproducibility. No finding identifies missing experimental protocol details; findings focus on data inconsistencies and reference errors, not protocol transparency.

Ground truth identifies overstated claims in Conclusion about 'significantly surpassing' literature and broad societal benefits without validation. No finding addresses these specific interpretive exaggerations in the Conclusion section.

Ground truth concerns fabricated citations and misattributions in Related Work (e.g., DLRT extended to federated learning by [36], UCM dataset inflation). Findings identify duplicate/missing citations but not the specific fabrications or misattributions described.

Ground truth identifies omission of ethical implications discussion (adversarial robustness risks, fairness, bias) in Experiments. No finding addresses missing ethical considerations; findings focus on technical and data inconsistencies.

Ground truth concerns promotional rhetorical manipulation in Introduction ('state-of-the-art,' 'significant progress') exaggerating impact. No finding identifies rhetorical tone issues; pred_id 18-19 address claim-result mismatches but not promotional language per se.

Ground truth identifies incoherence between regularizer assumptions (orthonormal U,V ensuring R(USV^T)=R(S)) and Algorithm 1's SVD truncation destroying orthogonality. No finding addresses this specific algorithmic inconsistency with theoretical assumptions.

Ground truth describes numerical manipulations in empirical tables (compression rates, accuracies adjusted by percentage points). pred_ids 6, 9, 12, 14 all identify specific numerical inconsistencies across tables (e.g., clean accuracy 94.61 vs 92.61, varying baseline values), matching the data integrity issue.

Ground truth identifies claim that RobustDLRT 'significantly outperforms' and 'almost doubles' baseline accuracy under Mixup, exaggerating small improvements. pred_id 7 identifies the specific '15% higher compression' claim being inconsistent with Table 4 data, capturing interpretation distortion of superiority claims.

Ground truth concerns asymmetric adversarial training exposure between RobustDLRT and baselines (unclear if identical adversarial batches used), violating fair comparison. No finding identifies this specific experimental design bias in adversarial training protocol.

Ground truth questions suspiciously low 3% training overhead on ImageNet given cubic cost in rank, with missing benchmarking details (batch size, hardware). No finding addresses the training time overhead claim or computational cost benchmarking integrity.

Ground truth identifies incoherence between Abstract's claim of model/data-agnostic universality and Method's restriction to Tucker factorization with specific assumptions. No finding addresses this Abstract-Method narrative inconsistency about architectural generality.

Ground truth concerns Appendix omitting ethical considerations statements (misuse, societal harms) beyond funding disclosure. No finding identifies missing ethical transparency in Acknowledgments/Disclosure section.
